Schedule billing reconciliation and SKU mapping call

Liam O'Connor | Deliver reference architecture diagram (initial) and deploy script | 2027-10-04

summary: Sync to align on marketplace listing requirements, reference architecture for AuroraCloud Marketplace, and joint solution packaging. Primary focus on VPC/private networking, SSO/SAML, KMS integration, and how billing/sku mapping will work in the marketplace. Agreed next steps to exchange artifacts and run a validation deploy in staging.
topics: Joint solution go-to-market and co-sell motion
Security & compliance: SSO, KMS, audit logs
transcript:
00:00 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, super appreciate it, we've got about an hour. quick intros?
00:08 Diego Martinez: Yeah Diego here, CTO at AuroraCloud, platform team lead, we own marketplace integrations.
00:13 Rina Patel: Rina, platform eng, I'll be owning the deploy bits.
:17 Maya Chen: Great, Liam O'Connor from Redwood is here to go through the reference arch and the packaging.
00:22 Liam O'Connor: Hey all, quick note I might talk a bit fast, sorry, uh, I have the template open.
00:30 Samir Kaur: Samir from partnerships, I'll handle listing approvals and marketing.
00:35 Alex: Alex legal (muffled) might drop in for the contract section.
00:40 Maya Chen: Cool, agenda, marketplace listing fields, reference arch for private/offered options, KMS/SSO, and next steps. any other items?
00:50 Diego Martinez: curious about dedicated vs hosted billing in the marketplace, how does SKU mapping work?
00:55 Liam O'Connor: good question; Redwood supports both hosted (we bill usage) and dedicated/reserved (we can attach subscription SKUs). typically marketplace requires a SKU per offer variant. we can produce a SKU mapping table, but need Aurora's marketplace product id and billing contact.
01:08 Rina Patel: for reference arch — we need to know if you're shipping a container, AMI, or integration connector; what's Redwood's recommended pattern for aurora's managed marketplace?
01:18 Liam O'Connor: recommended is a containerized connector with a small bootstrap that talks to the Redwood private control plane for auth. for private deployments in customer's VPC we provide an infra-as-code template and a sidecar connector. we also offer a marketplace listing where customers can click-to-deploy into their VPC using our helm chart or cloudformation.
01:33 Maya Chen: to add, for AuroraCloud Marketplace we typically publish two offers: "Redwood Hosted" (SaaS) and "Redwood Private Pack" (bring-your-own infra). the listing needs icons, short/long description, support SLA, and an install flow doc.
01:47 Diego Martinez: okay, for the Private Pack we need clear networking requirements — e.g., subnets, NAT, egress rules, and if we need a transit gateway.
01:56 Liam O'Connor: yes, we'll include a network appendix: required outbound ports (443 to redwood-control.redwood.ai and 3rd-party telemetry endpoints), optional inbound rules if using direct VPC peering, and guidance for KV cache placement. note: the transcript below has some typos, the automation tool sometimes swapped kv cache to tv cache.
02:18 Samir Kaur: on marketing side, we need a one-page joint solution brief with logos and a reference-arch diagram. can you deliver a PNG + editable svg?
02:25 Maya Chen: yes, we can. Liam will produce the initial diagram and we'll include alt text for accessibility.
02:33 Rina Patel: security: SSO and SAML — do you support SAML 2.0 from the marketplace for provisioning users?
02:40 Liam O'Connor: Redwood supports SAML 2.0 and OIDC; for marketplace we'd recommend SAML for SSO onboarding, and SCIM for provisioning if you want automated group sync. for private installs we support customer KMS (customer managed keys) — the template includes a KMS rotation note.
02:58 Diego Martinez: audit logs: we need to ensure logs can be shipped to Aurora's logging ingestion; are logs forwarded or do we provide an export?
03:05 Liam O'Connor: we support syslog/export and direct pushes to S3 or your logging endpoint; for hosted we can stream audit events to a customer-owned S3 bucket or SIEM via an authenticated connector.
03:20 Maya Chen: quick question on certifications — do we need SOC2/ISO statements in the listing? Aurora typically requires SOC2.
03:27 Diego Martinez: yes must have SOC2 type II and a whitepaper.
03:30 Maya Chen: Redwood has SOC2 Type II; we'll attach the cert and the attestation doc in the listing assets.
03:36 Alex (maybe mislabelled): legal question, marketplace contract — will it be Aurora's standard marketplace terms or custom?
03:41 Maya Chen: for most listings we take marketplace's standard terms, but for dedicated/reserved we sometimes sign a short addendum. we'll connect legal teams.
03:48 Samir Kaur: also want to call out co-sell motion: can Redwood include a joint case study or reference customers?
03:53 Maya Chen: yes, once the pilot is done we can put together a joint case study and co-marketing plan.
04:01 Rina Patel: operational question: how do upgrades work for the private package? can Redwood push upgrades or does Aurora orchestrate?
04:09 Liam O'Connor: by default, private packages are customer-controlled; we provide recommended upgrade manifests and an optional managed-upgrade service if you opt in. for marketplace we recommend customers subscribe to the managed updates or pin a version.
04:22 Diego Martinez: performance — can you share a profiling doc, latency numbers for typical token lengths? we want to set expectations for our customers who will run LLM features in our console.
04:31 Liam O'Connor: yes; Redwood ships benchmark profiles per model variant and sequence length. I'll attach the perf sheet; note: the sheet has breakdown by p50/p95/p99 latencies and token cost. also mention of KV cache behavior and batching impacts.
04:50 Maya Chen: good, now on deployment test plan — propose we do a validation deploy in Aurora staging on Tuesday, run a smoke test and a throughput profile against a synthetic workload.
05:00 Diego Martinez: Tuesday works for us, send the deploy PoC checklist.
05:05 Liam O'Connor: checklist items: staging VPC access, sample dataset, expected QPS, authorized SSH or CI service account, and monitoring endpoints. we'll provide a quick CLI to seed cache and run tokens.
05:20 Samir Kaur: marketing timeline — if we want the listing live by mid-Oct, assets and legal need to be done by early Oct. that's tight.
05:28 Maya Chen: agreed, timeline: draft listing by Oct 5, legal sync Oct 6-7, staging validation Oct 4-6, sign-off Oct 8, publish mid-Oct.
05:37 Rina Patel: small nit: your helm chart references a kubeFeatureGate name that we don't have enabled, we might need to adjust the chart — we'll flag exact error during staging.
05:48 Liam O'Connor: thanks, Rina, we'll fix the chart; small chance the automatic generator misnamed a flag — the transcript generator previously wrote "kube-guest" instead of real.
05:58 Diego Martinez: okay last thing, metrics and observability: do you export prometheus metrics or do we need a metrics adapter?
06:05 Liam O'Connor: we provide Prometheus metrics endpoint for the sidecar and a trace header for distributed tracing; we also have a small opamp for pushing metrics to a 3rd-party collector.
06:18 Maya Chen: awesome. let's recap next steps.
06:22 Maya Chen: recap — Redwood to share draft listing, reference arch, perf sheet, deploy scripts; Aurora to provide staging VPC and legal contact; schedule validation deploy next week.
06:35 Diego Martinez: sounds good, thanks everyone.
06:38 Samir Kaur: thanks all, will circulate marketing checklist.
06:41 Maya Chen: I'll follow up with an update thread and upload artifacts to the shared drive. meeting end.
